models.name: hrm_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts identified by device fingerprint for unauthenticated access.

Guest accounts enable device-based tracking and temporary session management without requiring email registration or password authentication. Each device is uniquely identified by its fingerprint, allowing the system to maintain continuity across browsing sessions for unauthenticated users.

**Identification**

The device_fingerprint field serves as the primary identifier for guest accounts, generated from browser and device characteristics. This enables recognition of returning devices without requiring user registration.

**Lifecycle**

Guest accounts support soft delete via the deleted_at field, allowing temporary deactivation while preserving historical data. Active guests have a null deleted_at value.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Unique identifier for each guest account.

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description:
Unique device fingerprint identifying the guest's device.

This field enables device-based identification without requiring user registration. Each device should have a unique fingerprint generated from browser/device characteristics such as user agent, screen resolution, installed fonts, and other browser APIs.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft-deleted. Null indicates active status.

models.name: hrm_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest device access with expiration.

This table stores authentication session records for guest users who access the system without creating a full member account. Each session is tied to a specific guest device and includes metadata for security auditing.

Session Lifecycle

Sessions are created when a guest device first accesses the system and are automatically invalidated after expiration. The expired_at field is NOT NULL to enforce explicit session timeout policies.

Security Considerations

Each session tracks the originating IP address, href, and referrer for audit purposes. Sessions belong to exactly one {@link hrm_guests} record and support multiple concurrent sessions per guest device.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the session record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_guest_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the guest account that owns this session.

This foreign key establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_guests}, ensuring each session belongs to exactly one guest device. The guest record is identified by device fingerprint and temporary credentials.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description:
IP address of the client device that created this session.

Used for security auditing and detecting suspicious access patterns from different locations.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description:
The href URL where the session was initiated.

Tracks the entry point of the guest session for analytics and security purposes.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description:
The referrer URL that led to this session creation.

Captures the source page or external link that directed the guest to the system.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this session was created.

Marks the beginning of the session lifecycle.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this session expires and becomes invalid.

This field is NOT NULL to enforce explicit session timeout policies. Sessions beyond this timestamp are automatically considered invalid.

models.name: hrm_members
models.description:
Member user accounts with email/password authentication credentials and global profile data.

This table represents the core actor entity for authenticated users in the system. Each member has a unique email address for login and a securely hashed password. The global profile data is stored here and shared across all organizations the user belongs to.

Authentication: Members authenticate using email and password credentials. The password_hash field stores a bcrypt hash of the user's password for secure authentication.

Soft Delete Support: The deleted_at field enables soft deletion, allowing member accounts to be deactivated without permanent data loss. When deleted_at is null, the account is active.

Multi-Organization Membership: Members can belong to multiple organizations through the hrm_employees table, which links members to organizations with role and department assignments.

Account Lifecycle: Members can delete their accounts, subject to constraints around organization ownership and employee records in other organizations.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key identifier for the member account.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
Unique email address for authentication.

This field serves as the primary identifier for member login. It must be unique across all member accounts and is used for authentication, password reset, and email verification flows.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description:
Bcrypt hash of the user's password.

The password is never stored in plain text. This field contains the securely hashed password using bcrypt or equivalent algorithm for authentication.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the account was created.

Set automatically upon account registration. Used for audit trails and account age calculations.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the account was last updated.

Automatically updated on any modification to the account. Used for tracking account changes and synchronization.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the account was soft-deleted. Null if active.

When set, the account is considered deleted but data is retained. This enables account recovery and audit compliance. Null value indicates an active account.

models.name: hrm_member_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh token support.

This table tracks authenticated member sessions and their lifecycle. Each session contains JWT tokens for API authentication and metadata about the session origin.

## Session Lifecycle

Sessions are created upon successful member login and expire based on configured token expiration policies. Sessions are append-only audit trails managed exclusively through authentication flows.

## Security Considerations

Sessions include IP address and referrer information for security auditing. The expired_at field enforces session expiration and is NOT NULL by default to ensure all sessions have defined lifecycles.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the session record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the member user who owns this session.

Each session belongs to exactly one {@link hrm_members} record. Multiple sessions may exist for the same member across different devices or browsers.

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description:
JWT access token for API authentication.

This token is used to authenticate API requests and contains claims about the member's identity and permissions. Tokens are short-lived and must be refreshed periodically.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description:
JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token is used to generate new access tokens when the current one expires. Refresh tokens have longer lifespans than access tokens and are rotated on use for security.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description:
IP address of the client that created this session.

Used for security auditing and detecting suspicious session activity from unusual locations.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description:
Current page URL (href) when session was created.

Captures the page context where the user initiated the login or session refresh.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description:
Referrer URL when session was created.

Tracks the source page that led to the authentication action.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this session was created.

Used for session ordering and calculating session age.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this session expires.

Sessions are invalidated after this timestamp. This field is NOT NULL to enforce explicit session expiration policies.

models.name: hrm_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for member account recovery with expiration and single-use constraint.

This table stores one-time use tokens that members can use to reset their passwords. Each token is valid for a limited time and becomes invalid after use.

## Token Lifecycle

Tokens are created when a member requests a password reset. The token is sent via email and must be used within the expiration period. Once used, the token is marked as consumed and cannot be reused.

## Security Constraints

- Tokens are single-use only
- Tokens expire after a configured time period
- Multiple tokens can exist for the same member, but only unexpired, unused tokens are valid
- Old tokens are cleaned up via scheduled job

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key identifier for this password reset token record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the member account requesting password reset.

This foreign key links the reset token to the specific member whose password will be reset. The member must exist in {@link hrm_members} table.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description:
Unique cryptographic token sent to member's email for password reset.

This token is generated using a secure random algorithm and is unique across all password reset requests. It must be included in the password reset request URL.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this token becomes invalid.

Tokens are automatically considered invalid after this time. A background job should periodically delete expired tokens to maintain table cleanliness.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this token was consumed for password reset.

Once this field is populated, the token cannot be used again. This enforces the single-use constraint. Null indicates the token is still valid for use.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was soft-deleted.

models.name: hrm_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for member registration with expiration and single-use constraint.

This table stores temporary verification tokens sent to users during registration to confirm email ownership. Each token is valid for a limited time and can only be used once.

**Token Lifecycle**
- Created when user registers or requests email verification
- Sent via email to the user
- Validated when user clicks verification link
- Marked as used after successful verification
- Expired tokens are cleaned up periodically

**Security Constraints**
- Single-use: token is invalidated after first use
- Expiration: tokens expire after configured time period
- Unique token per verification request

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the email verification record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_member_id

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description:
Unique verification token sent to the user's email address.

This is a cryptographically secure random string used to validate email ownership. The token is included in the verification email link and must match exactly for verification to succeed.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
Email address being verified.

Stored for reference and to allow re-sending verification emails. This should match the email provided during member registration.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the verification token expires.

Tokens are invalidated after this time to prevent reuse of old verification links. Typical expiration is 24 hours from creation.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the token was successfully used for verification.

This field is null until the user completes email verification. Once set, the token cannot be used again (single-use constraint).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification record was soft-deleted.

models.name: hrm_organizations
models.description:
Organization entities with multi-tenancy configuration including name, description, logo, currency, timezone, and fiscal period settings.

Organizations serve as the foundational isolation boundary for all business data. Each organization operates independently with its own configuration settings, employees, projects, and time tracking records.

**Configuration Fields**
- Currency: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW) for financial calculations
- Timezone: IANA timezone identifier for date/time formatting
- Fiscal Start Month: Month number (1-12) defining the organization's fiscal year

**Deletion Constraints**
- Cannot delete if pending timesheets exist (not approved or rejected)
- Cannot delete if active employee contracts exist
- Cascades to all employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets
- Owner accounts remain but are disassociated from the deleted organization

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the organization record.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Organization display name.

Required for identification and user-facing references.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Organization description or tagline.

Optional field for additional context about the organization.

plainFields.name: logo_image_url
plainFields.description:
URL to organization logo image.

Used for branding in user interfaces and communications.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description:
ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW).

Used for all financial calculations including contract pay rates and project budgets.

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description:
IANA timezone identifier (e.g., America/New_York, Asia/Seoul).

Used for date/time formatting and timesheet week boundaries.

plainFields.name: fiscal_start_month
plainFields.description:
Fiscal year start month (1-12).

January=1, December=12. Used for financial reporting periods.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Record creation timestamp.

Automatically set on organization creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Record last update timestamp.

Automatically updated on any field modification.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Soft delete timestamp.

When null, organization is active. When set, organization is marked for deletion but retained for audit purposes.

models.name: hrm_organization_owners
models.description:
Organization ownership tracking with current and historical owner records to support ownership transfer lifecycle

This table maintains a complete audit trail of organization ownership changes, enabling ownership transfer workflows and historical analysis. Each organization can have multiple ownership records over time, but only one current owner at any given point.

Ownership Lifecycle

When an organization is created, an initial ownership record is created with is_current=true and ended_at=NULL. When ownership is transferred, the current record's ended_at is set to the transfer date and is_current=false, while a new record is created for the new owner. When an organization is deleted, all ownership records are cascade deleted.

Data Integrity

Application-level enforcement ensures only one current owner per organization (is_current=true with ended_at=NULL). The unique constraint on (organization_id, is_current) prevents duplicate current or historical flags, while business logic ensures single current ownership.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each ownership record.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the organization whose ownership is being tracked.

This foreign key establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_organizations}. Ownership records cannot exist without a valid organization. When an organization is deleted, all associated ownership records are cascade deleted per multi-tenancy data isolation rules.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the user who owns or owned the organization.

This foreign key establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_members}. Users can own multiple organizations over time, creating separate ownership records for each. When a user account is deleted, ownership records are handled per account deletion constraints (must transfer ownership or delete organization first if sole owner).

plainFields.name: is_current
plainFields.description:
Flag indicating whether this is the current active ownership record.

When true, this record represents the active owner of the organization. Only one record per organization should have is_current=true at any time. Application logic enforces this constraint during ownership transfers.

Current ownership: is_current=true, ended_at=NULL
Historical ownership: is_current=false, ended_at=transfer date

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this ownership record became effective.

For initial ownership, this is the organization creation time. For transferred ownership, this is the transfer date. This field is never null and establishes the ownership period start.

plainFields.name: ended_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this ownership record became inactive (NULL if currently active).

When NULL, indicates this is the current ownership record. When set, indicates the ownership ended due to transfer or organization deletion. This field enables historical ownership queries and audit trails.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last updated. Updated during ownership transfers when ended_at is set.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was soft deleted. NULL if the record is active. Used for audit trail preservation before cascade deletion.

models.name: hrm_organization_roles
models.description:
Organization-specific roles including built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) and custom roles defined by organization owners.

Role Types

Built-in roles (is_builtin=true) are system-defined and cannot be deleted: Owner, Manager, Employee. Custom roles (is_builtin=false) can be created and deleted by organization owners, subject to assignment constraints.

Deletion Constraints

Built-in roles cannot be deleted under any circumstances. Custom roles cannot be deleted if employees are currently assigned to them. This ensures role assignments remain valid.

Organization Scope

Each role belongs to exactly one {@link HrmOrganizations} and is visible only within that organization's context. Role names must be unique within each organization to prevent ambiguity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the role record.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description:
References the organization this role belongs to.

Each role is scoped to exactly one organization and inherits the organization's data isolation boundaries. Role permissions and assignments are valid only within this organization context.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Role name within the organization.

Must be unique within the organization (enforced by unique index). Built-in roles use fixed names: Owner, Manager, Employee. Custom roles can use any descriptive name chosen by the organization owner.

plainFields.name: is_builtin
plainFields.description:
Indicates whether this is a system-built-in role.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot be deleted and have fixed permission sets. Custom roles created by organization owners have is_builtin=false and can be modified or deleted if not assigned to employees.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the role was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the role was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the role was soft-deleted (nullable for active roles).

models.name: hrm_departments
models.description:
Department structure within organizations supporting one-level nesting via parent department reference

This table organizes employees into hierarchical department groups within each organization. Departments support a single level of nesting where a department can have one parent department but multiple child departments.

Department Lifecycle

Departments are created by organization administrators and can be deleted. When a department is deleted, all employees assigned to it have their department_id set to null rather than being deleted themselves. This preserves employee records while removing the department grouping.

Soft deletion is supported via the deleted_at field, allowing departments to be hidden without permanent data loss.

Hierarchy Constraints

The parent_department_id field enables one-level nesting only. A department can reference another department in the same organization as its parent, but nested hierarchies beyond one level are not supported. This keeps the department structure flat and manageable.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each department record

foreignFields.name: organization_id
parent_department_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the parent department for one-level hierarchy nesting

This self-referencing foreign key allows a department to have one parent department within the same organization. Null value indicates a top-level department with no parent.

Only one level of nesting is supported - child departments cannot have their own children.

{@link hrm_departments}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Department name displayed to users

Must be unique within the organization. Common examples include "Engineering", "Human Resources", "Sales", "Marketing".

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description of the department's purpose and responsibilities

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was created

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was last updated

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was soft-deleted. Null if the department is active.

models.name: hrm_employees
models.description:
Employee records linking users to organizations with role, department, position, employment type, and status.

This table represents the employment relationship between a user and an organization. Each employee record connects a user account to their role within a specific organization, capturing their position, employment type, and current status.

**Relationships**

- {@link hrm_organizations}: Each employee belongs to exactly one organization. Organization deletion cascades to all employee records.
- {@link hrm_members}: Each employee links to exactly one user account. A user can have multiple employee records across different organizations.
- {@link hrm_roles}: Each employee has exactly one role within their organization. Role changes are tracked through role_id updates.
- {@link hrm_departments}: Employees may optionally belong to a department within their organization. Department is nullable to support employees without department assignment.

**Business Rules**

- One employee record per user per organization (enforced by unique constraint on organization_id and user_id)
- Status field controls employee lifecycle: active employees can log time and access organization resources; deactivated employees lose access but records are preserved
- Employment type categorizes the nature of employment: full-time, part-time, contractor, or intern
- Soft delete support via deleted_at field for employee record archival

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each employee record.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description:
References the organization this employee belongs to.

Each employee is associated with exactly one organization. All employee data is scoped to their organization for multi-tenancy isolation.

**Business Rules**

- Required field - every employee must belong to an organization
- Organization deletion cascades to all employee records
- Employee can only access data within their organization context

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description:
References the user account associated with this employee record.

Links the employee record to the global user account ({@link hrm_members}). A single user can have multiple employee records across different organizations.

**Business Rules**

- Required field - every employee must be linked to a user account
- One employee record per user per organization (unique constraint)
- User account deletion deactivates all associated employee records

foreignFields.name: role_id
foreignFields.description:
References the role assigned to this employee within their organization.

Defines the employee's permissions and access level within the organization. Each employee has exactly one role at a time.

**Business Rules**

- Required field - every employee must have a role
- Role changes update this field directly
- Custom roles cannot be deleted if employees are assigned to them
- Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) always available

foreignFields.name: department_id
foreignFields.description:
References the department this employee belongs to within their organization.

Optional department assignment for organizational hierarchy. Employees can exist without department assignment.

**Business Rules**

- Nullable field - employees may not belong to any department
- Department deletion sets this field to null (does not delete employee)
- Supports one-level department nesting through department's parent_department_id

plainFields.name: position
plainFields.description:
Job title or position name for this employee.

Captures the employee's specific role or title within the organization (e.g., "Senior Developer", "Marketing Manager", "HR Specialist").

plainFields.name: employment_type
plainFields.description:
Type of employment arrangement for this employee.

**Allowed Values**

- `full-time`: Standard full-time employment
- `part-time`: Part-time employment with reduced hours
- `contractor`: Contract-based worker
- `intern`: Internship position

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current employment status of this employee.

**Allowed Values**

- `active`: Employee is currently active and can access organization resources
- `deactivated`: Employee has been deactivated (loses access but record preserved)

**Business Rules**

- Status changes affect employee access to organization features
- Deactivated employees cannot log time or access protected resources
- Status can be reactivated for former employees returning to the organization

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this employee record was created.

Recorded automatically upon employee creation for audit trail purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this employee record was last updated.

Updated automatically on any modification to the employee record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this employee record was soft-deleted.

Null while employee is active or deactivated. Set to current timestamp when employee is deleted, enabling soft delete functionality for record preservation.

models.name: hrm_employee_invitations
models.description:
Pending invitations for users to join organizations with email, role, and invitation status tracking

Invitations are created by organization members to invite new employees to join their organization. Each invitation specifies the target organization, the role to assign upon acceptance, and an expiration date. When an invited user signs up with the matching email address, they can accept the invitation and be automatically added as an employee with the specified role.

Invitation Lifecycle:
- Pending: Invitation sent, awaiting user acceptance via email token
- Accepted: User has signed up and accepted the invitation, employee record created
- Expired: Invitation past expiration date, cannot be accepted
- Cancelled: Manually cancelled by the inviter before acceptance

The invited_by field tracks which member sent the invitation for audit purposes. The member_id field is populated when the invited user accepts the invitation, creating the link between the invitation and the actual member account.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the invitation record.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Organization the invited user will join.

Each invitation is scoped to a specific organization and cannot be transferred between organizations. The organization must exist and be active when the invitation is created.

foreignFields.name: role_id
foreignFields.description:
Role assigned to the invited user upon acceptance.

The role must exist within the target organization. Both built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) and custom roles defined by the organization are supported. The role determines the permissions the new employee will have.

foreignFields.name: invited_by_id
foreignFields.description:
Member who created and sent this invitation.

Tracks which organization member initiated the invitation for audit and accountability purposes. This references the hrm_members table, representing the authenticated user who sent the invitation.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description:
Member who accepted this invitation.

Remains null while the invitation is pending. Populated with the member ID when the invited user signs up and accepts the invitation via the unique token. This creates the link between the invitation and the actual member account.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
Email address of the invited user.

Used to match the invitation when the user signs up. The invited user must register with this exact email address to accept the invitation. Combined with organization_id and status, ensures only one pending invitation per email per organization.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current status of the invitation.

Allowed values:
- pending: Invitation sent, awaiting acceptance via email token
- accepted: User has signed up and accepted the invitation, employee record created
- expired: Invitation past expiration date, cannot be accepted
- cancelled: Manually cancelled by the inviter before acceptance

Status transitions: pending → accepted, pending → expired, pending → cancelled. Once accepted, expired, or cancelled, the invitation cannot be reactivated.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description:
Unique token for invitation acceptance.

Generated when the invitation is created and sent to the invited user's email address. Used to verify and accept the invitation securely. Must be unique across all invitations to prevent token collision attacks.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description:
Expiration date and time for the invitation.

Invitations become invalid after this timestamp and cannot be accepted. Expired invitations remain in the database for audit purposes but are filtered out from active invitation lists. Typical expiration is 7-30 days from creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was last updated, such as when status changed or member_id was populated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the invitation was soft-deleted.

Soft deletes allow audit trail preservation while hiding invitations from active queries. Typically used for compliance or data retention policies.

models.name: hrm_employee_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of employee records for audit trail and change tracking

This table captures historical states of employee records at specific moments in time. Each snapshot represents the complete state of an employee record when it was created, enabling audit trails and change tracking across the organization.

Snapshots are immutable once created and serve as a read-only historical record. They reference the original employee record through a foreign key relationship, allowing reconstruction of employee states at any point in time.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the snapshot record

foreignFields.name: hrm_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the employee record being snapshot

This foreign key links the snapshot to its source employee record in {@link HrmEmployees}. The relationship is one-to-many, as an employee can have multiple snapshots over time.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Organization identifier denormalized from the employee record

This field captures the organization context at the time of the snapshot, enabling historical queries even if the employee's organization changes.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description:
User identifier denormalized from the employee record

This field captures the user association at the time of the snapshot, enabling historical queries even if the employee's user association changes.

foreignFields.name: role_id
foreignFields.description:
Role identifier denormalized from the employee record

This field captures the role assignment at the time of the snapshot, enabling historical queries even if the employee's role changes.

foreignFields.name: department_id
foreignFields.description:
Department identifier denormalized from the employee record

This field captures the department assignment at the time of the snapshot, enabling historical queries even if the employee's department changes.

plainFields.name: position
plainFields.description:
Employee position/title denormalized from the employee record

Captures the position at the time of snapshot for historical tracking.

plainFields.name: employment_type
plainFields.description:
Employment type denormalized from the employee record

Values: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern. Captures the employment type at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Employee status denormalized from the employee record

Values: active, deactivated. Captures the status at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot was created

Records the point-in-time when this historical record was captured.

models.name: hrm_roles
models.description:
Organization-specific roles including built-in (Owner, Manager, Employee) and custom roles.

Built-in roles cannot be deleted; custom roles cannot be deleted if employees are assigned.

## Role Types

**Built-in Roles**: Three system-defined roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) that exist in every organization and cannot be deleted. These roles have predefined permission sets.

**Custom Roles**: Organization-defined roles created by organization owners to implement custom permission configurations. Custom roles can be deleted only if no employees are assigned to them.

## Business Constraints

- Role names must be unique within each organization
- Built-in roles have `is_builtin = true` and cannot be deleted
- Custom roles (`is_builtin = false`) cannot be deleted if any {@link hrm_employees} reference them
- Soft delete via `deleted_at` preserves historical role assignments

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each role record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
References the organization this role belongs to. Roles are scoped to a single organization and cannot be shared across organizations.

Each role must belong to exactly one {@link hrm_organizations}. This foreign key enforces data isolation between organizations.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Role name unique within the organization.

Built-in roles use fixed names: "Owner", "Manager", "Employee". Custom roles can have any name chosen by the organization owner.

plainFields.name: is_builtin
plainFields.description:
Indicates whether this is a system-defined built-in role.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) have `is_builtin = true` and cannot be deleted. Custom roles have `is_builtin = false` and can be deleted if no employees are assigned.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Optional description explaining the role's purpose and responsibilities.

Custom roles typically include descriptions to help organization members understand the role's scope. Built-in roles may have system-generated descriptions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this role was created.

Built-in roles are created automatically when an organization is initialized. Custom roles are created when organization owners define new role configurations.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this role was last modified.

Updated whenever role properties (name, description) are changed. Built-in role properties typically cannot be modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this role was soft-deleted.

Custom roles can be soft-deleted when no longer needed, preserving historical employee assignments. Built-in roles cannot be deleted. Null indicates the role is active.

models.name: hrm_permissions
models.description:
Permission definitions available for assignment to roles within the HRM system.

This table stores system-defined permission names that control access to various features and operations. Each permission represents a specific capability that can be granted to roles.

Permission Categories

Organization permissions: org:manage - Full organization configuration and lifecycle management

Employee permissions: employee:manage - Create, edit, deactivate employees; employee:view - View employee records and details

Project permissions: project:manage - Create, edit, archive projects; project:view - View project information and member lists

Time permissions: time:manage - Create, edit, delete timelogs; time:approve - Approve or reject timesheets; time:view_all - View all timelogs across the organization

Reporting permissions: report:view - Access organization-wide reports and analytics

Usage

Permissions are assigned to roles through the {@link hrm_role_permissions} junction table. Roles then grant these permissions to employees within an organization. The permission names follow a {domain}:{action} naming convention for clarity and consistency.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each permission definition.

plainFields.name: permission_name
plainFields.description:
Unique permission identifier following {domain}:{action} convention.

Examples: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of what this permission allows users to do.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission definition was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission definition was last updated.

models.name: hrm_role_permissions
models.description:
Junction table assigning permissions to roles. Each role must have at least one permission. Custom roles require at least one permission to be created.

This table establishes the many-to-many relationship between roles and permissions within an organization. It enforces that every role has at least one permission assigned, and custom roles cannot be created without permissions.

Relationships:
- Each record links one {@link hrm_roles} to one {@link hrm_permissions}
- A role can have multiple permissions
- A permission can be assigned to multiple roles
- Composite unique constraint prevents duplicate role-permission assignments

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each role-permission assignment record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_role_id
foreignFields.description:
References the role to which this permission is assigned. Each role must have at least one permission assigned.

This foreign key establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_roles} and enforces referential integrity. Cascade delete ensures permissions are removed when a role is deleted.

foreignFields.name: hrm_permission_id
foreignFields.description:
References the permission assigned to the role. Each permission can be assigned to multiple roles.

This foreign key establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_permissions} and enforces referential integrity. Cascade delete ensures role-permission assignments are removed when a permission is deleted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this role-permission assignment was created. Automatically set on record creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this role-permission assignment was last updated. Automatically updated on record modification.

models.name: hrm_contracts
models.description:
Employment contracts tracking compensation and terms for employees with lifecycle states.

Each contract records the financial and working terms between an employee and their organization. The contract lifecycle is managed through start_date and end_date fields, where a NULL end_date indicates an active contract. Application logic enforces that only one active contract exists per employee at any time.

**Lifecycle Management**

When a new contract is created, the system automatically terminates the previous active contract by setting its end_date to one day before the new contract's start_date. This ensures a continuous employment history without gaps. Once a contract's end_date is set, the record becomes immutable to preserve historical accuracy for audit and compliance purposes.

**Compensation Details**

The contract captures pay_rate as a numeric value, pay_period as a categorical value (hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly), and working_hours_per_week as an optional numeric field. These fields support payroll calculations and employment verification across different employment types including full-time, part-time, contractor, and intern arrangements.

**Relationships**

Each contract belongs to exactly one {@link hrm_employees} record through the hrm_employee_id foreign key. The contract is a subsidiary entity that cannot exist independently of its parent employee record. When an employee is deleted, all associated contracts are cascade deleted to maintain referential integrity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each employment contract record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
References the employee record to which this contract belongs. Each employee can have multiple contracts over time, but only one active contract (NULL end_date) at any given time.

**Relationship**

This foreign key establishes a many-to-one relationship from contracts to employees. The hrm_employees table is the parent entity, and contracts are managed through the employee context.

**Constraints**

This field is NOT NULL, ensuring every contract is associated with a valid employee record. Cascade delete is applied when the parent employee is removed.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description:
The effective start date of this employment contract. Marks when the contractual terms become active.

**Business Rule**

This field is required and cannot be null. When creating a new contract, the system validates that the start_date does not overlap with existing active contracts for the same employee.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description:
The effective end date of this employment contract. A NULL value indicates the contract is currently active.

**Business Rule**

When a new contract is created for an employee, the previous active contract's end_date is automatically set to one day before the new contract's start_date. Once end_date is populated, the contract becomes immutable to preserve historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: pay_rate
plainFields.description:
The compensation rate specified in this contract. The actual unit (per hour, day, week, or month) is determined by the pay_period field.

**Usage**

This numeric value is used for payroll calculations, budget tracking, and employment verification. The value should be stored in the organization's base currency.

plainFields.name: pay_period
plainFields.description:
The frequency at which the pay_rate is applied. Valid values are: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly.

**Enumeration**

- hourly: Pay rate per hour worked
- daily: Pay rate per day worked
- weekly: Pay rate per week
- monthly: Pay rate per month

This field determines how the pay_rate value should be interpreted for payroll calculations.

plainFields.name: working_hours_per_week
plainFields.description:
The expected number of working hours per week under this contract. Optional field for contracts where hourly tracking is relevant.

**Usage**

This value is used for full-time vs part-time classification, overtime calculations, and compliance with labor regulations. May be null for contractor or irregular work arrangements.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description:
Optional text field for additional contract terms, special conditions, or administrative notes not captured in structured fields.

**Usage**

This field stores free-form text for edge cases or custom arrangements that don't fit the standard contract schema. Examples include remote work agreements, bonus structures, or special benefits.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this contract record was created in the system. Used for audit trail and record-keeping purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this contract record was last modified. Updated automatically on any change to the contract fields.

**Immutability**

Once end_date is set (contract terminated), this field should not change as the record becomes immutable.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this contract was soft-deleted. NULL indicates the record is active in the system.

**Usage**

Soft delete allows contracts to be marked for deletion while preserving historical data for audit purposes. Cascade delete applies when the parent employee is removed.

models.name: hrm_contract_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of contract changes for audit trail and historical tracking.

This table captures immutable versions of {@link hrm_contracts} at specific moments, enabling audit trails and historical analysis of contract modifications. Each snapshot preserves the complete state of a contract including compensation terms, employment dates, and work arrangements.

**Snapshot Behavior**

Snapshots are created automatically when contracts are modified, providing a complete history of changes over time. The table is append-only and read-only from a user perspective, with no update or delete operations permitted.

**Relationship to Contracts**

Each snapshot references exactly one {@link hrm_contracts} record via hrm_contract_id. Multiple snapshots can exist for the same contract, representing different points in time as the contract evolves through its lifecycle.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each contract snapshot record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_contract_id
foreignFields.description:
References the parent contract record that this snapshot captures.

Each snapshot is tied to exactly one {@link hrm_contracts} record, preserving the contract's state at the time the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: employee_id
plainFields.description: Employee identifier at the time of snapshot, denormalized from the parent contract for historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Contract start date as recorded when the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description: Contract end date as recorded when the snapshot was created. Null indicates an ongoing active contract.

plainFields.name: pay_rate
plainFields.description: Compensation rate (hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly) as recorded when the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: pay_period
plainFields.description: Pay period type: hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly. Captured at snapshot creation time.

plainFields.name: working_hours_per_week
plainFields.description: Expected weekly working hours as recorded when the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Additional contract notes or special terms as recorded when the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, marking the point-in-time of the captured contract state.

models.name: hrm_projects
models.description:
Main project entity with organization, name, color, status, and timeline.

Projects represent work initiatives within an organization. Each project has a name, optional description, visual color code for UI identification, and lifecycle status. Projects track budget hours and timeline dates for planning purposes.

**Status Lifecycle**

Projects transition through three states: active (current work), archived (inactive but preserved), and completed (finished work). Archived and completed projects cannot receive new timelogs but existing timelogs are preserved for historical records.

**Deletion Constraints**

Projects cannot be deleted if timelogs exist. Soft delete is supported via deleted_at field for recovery purposes. Use status transitions (archived/completed) instead of deletion for most lifecycle management.

**Relationships**

Projects belong to {@link hrm_organizations} and contain {@link hrm_tasks}, {@link hrm_timelogs}, and {@link hrm_project_members}. Project members link employees to projects with role assignments.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key identifier for the project.

foreignFields.name: hrm_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
References the organization that owns this project.

Every project must belong to exactly one organization. Organization context is enforced on all project operations for multi-tenancy data isolation.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Project name for display and identification.

Required field used throughout the UI for project references and navigation.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Detailed description of the project scope and objectives.

Optional field providing additional context about project goals, deliverables, and requirements.

plainFields.name: color_code
plainFields.description:
Hex color code for visual identification in UI.

Used for project badges, timeline indicators, and dashboard visualizations. Format: #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current project status: active, archived, or completed.

Active projects accept new timelogs and task assignments. Archived projects are inactive but preserved for historical reference. Completed projects are finished and cannot receive new timelogs.

plainFields.name: budget_hours
plainFields.description:
Estimated budget hours for the project.

Optional planning field tracking allocated time resources. Used for capacity planning and progress tracking against estimates.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description:
Planned or actual project start date.

Optional field marking when project work began or is scheduled to begin.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description:
Planned or actual project completion date.

Optional field marking when project is expected to finish or has finished.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the project was soft deleted.

Null for active projects. Set to current timestamp when project is soft deleted for recovery purposes.

models.name: hrm_project_members
models.description:
Links employees to projects with role assignment (member or project-lead).

This junction table establishes the many-to-many relationship between {@link hrm_employees} and {@link hrm_projects}. Each record represents an employee's assignment to a specific project with an associated role that determines their permissions within that project context.

**Role Assignment**

The role field specifies the employee's capacity within the project. Project leads have elevated permissions to manage tasks and oversee project activities, while regular members have standard access to contribute to project work. This role-based access control is enforced at the application layer.

**Relationship Constraints**

Each employee can be assigned to multiple projects, and each project can have multiple employees. A unique constraint on the combination of project_id and employee_id ensures that an employee cannot be assigned to the same project more than once, preventing duplicate records and maintaining data integrity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each project member assignment record.

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description:
References the project this member assignment belongs to.

Establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_projects}. This foreign key ensures referential integrity and enables querying all members of a specific project.

foreignFields.name: employee_id
foreignFields.description:
References the employee assigned to this project.

Establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_employees}. This foreign key enables querying all projects an employee is assigned to across the organization.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description:
The employee's role within this project.

Allowed values:
- `member`: Standard project member with basic access permissions
- `project-lead`: Project lead with elevated permissions to manage tasks and oversee project activities

This field determines the access control level for the employee within the project context.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this project member assignment was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this project member assignment was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this project member assignment was soft-deleted. Null indicates the assignment is active.

models.name: hrm_tasks
models.description:
Tasks within projects with status, priority, assignment, and one-level nesting support.

This table represents individual work items that belong to projects. Each task can have a status indicating its progress, a priority level for scheduling, optional time estimates, and due dates. Tasks can be assigned to employees and support one-level parent-child nesting for subtasks.

**Status Workflow**
Tasks progress through states: open → in-progress → completed → closed. Status changes are logged in {@link hrm_task_histories} for audit purposes.

**Assignment**
Tasks can be assigned to employees within the organization. Unassigned tasks remain available for assignment by project members with appropriate permissions.

**Parent-Child Relationship**
The parent_task_id field enables one-level task nesting for subtasks. A task can have at most one parent but can have multiple children. This supports hierarchical task breakdown without deep nesting complexity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each task.

foreignFields.name: project_id
assigned_employee_id
parent_task_id

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Short descriptive title of the task.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the task requirements and context.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current workflow state of the task.

Allowed values: open, in-progress, completed, closed.

Status transitions are logged in {@link hrm_task_histories} for audit trail.

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description:
Priority level for task scheduling and visibility.

Allowed values: low, medium, high, urgent.

Higher priority tasks appear first in task lists and dashboards.

plainFields.name: estimated_hours
plainFields.description:
Estimated time to complete the task in hours.

Used for project planning and capacity forecasting. Nullable for tasks where estimation is not available or not applicable.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description:
Target completion date for the task.

Used for deadline tracking and overdue notifications. Nullable for tasks without a specific deadline.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was soft-deleted. Null indicates active task.

models.name: hrm_task_histories
models.description:
Audit trail for task status changes with timestamp and user who made the change.

This table records every status transition for tasks, creating an immutable history of task lifecycle events. Each row captures the before and after status values along with the timestamp and the member who initiated the change.

**Relationships**

- References {@link hrm_tasks} to identify which task was modified
- References {@link hrm_members} to identify the user who made the change

**Usage**

- Audit trail for compliance and debugging
- Track task workflow progression over time
- Identify who made specific status changes

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for this audit record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_task_id
foreignFields.description:
References the task whose status was changed.

This foreign key establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_tasks}, linking each history record to its parent task. Multiple history records can reference the same task, creating a chronological audit trail.

foreignFields.name: hrm_member_id
foreignFields.description:
References the member who made the status change.

This foreign key links to {@link hrm_members} to identify which authenticated user initiated the task status transition. This enables accountability and audit capabilities.

plainFields.name: timestamp
plainFields.description:
The exact time when the task status change occurred.

This field captures the precise moment of the status transition, enabling chronological ordering of task history events.

plainFields.name: old_status
plainFields.description:
The task status before the change.

Stores the previous status value (e.g., 'open', 'in-progress', 'completed', 'closed') to enable comparison and audit of status transitions.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description:
The task status after the change.

Stores the new status value (e.g., 'open', 'in-progress', 'completed', 'closed') to complete the status transition record.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this audit record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this audit record was last updated.

models.name: hrm_timelogs
models.description:
Individual time entries with project, task, and billable tracking.

Stores granular time tracking records for employee work activities. Each timelog represents a discrete work session with associated project, optional task, duration, and billable status. Timelogs are aggregated into timesheets for weekly reporting and approval workflows.

Relationships: Each timelog belongs to exactly one {@link hrm_employees} record, one {@link hrm_projects} record, and optionally one {@link hrm_tasks} record. Billable flag determines if time is chargeable to clients.

Constraints: Timelogs cannot be edited or deleted if included in approved timesheets. Users with time:manage permission can override these restrictions.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each timelog entry.

foreignFields.name: hrm_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the employee who created this timelog. Each timelog is owned by exactly one employee and cannot be transferred.

This foreign key establishes the ownership relationship to {@link hrm_employees}. Employees can only create timelogs for themselves, enforced at the application layer.

foreignFields.name: hrm_project_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the project this timelog belongs to. All time entries must be associated with a project for proper tracking and reporting.

This foreign key establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_projects}. Project status (archived/completed) affects whether new timelogs can be created.

foreignFields.name: hrm_task_id
foreignFields.description:
Optional reference to the specific task this timelog is associated with. Tasks provide granular breakdown of work within projects.

This foreign key establishes an optional relationship to {@link hrm_tasks}. Timelogs can exist without task assignment for general project work.

plainFields.name: date
plainFields.description:
The calendar date when the work was performed. Used for grouping timelogs into weekly timesheets.

Stored as datetime with time component set to midnight for consistency. Indexed for efficient date range queries.

plainFields.name: duration_minutes
plainFields.description:
Total duration of work in minutes. Represents the actual time spent on the project/task.

Calculated from timer sessions or manually entered. Rounded to nearest minute for consistency.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Optional notes describing the work performed. Provides context for the time entry beyond project/task assignment.

Free-form text field for additional details about the work activity.

plainFields.name: billable
plainFields.description:
Flag indicating whether this time entry is billable to clients. Determines if time is chargeable or internal.

Defaults to true. Non-billable time is typically internal work, training, or administrative tasks.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timelog record was created. Used for audit trail and sorting.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timelog record was last modified. Updated on any field change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this timelog was soft-deleted. Null for active records.

Soft delete preserves timelogs that may be referenced by timesheets while hiding them from active queries.

models.name: hrm_timesheets
models.description:
Weekly time summaries with approval workflow and review tracking.

This table captures employee timesheets organized by week, tracking time entry aggregations through an approval workflow. Each timesheet represents a week of work (Monday to Sunday) and transitions through draft, submitted, approved, or rejected states.

Workflow States

Timesheets progress through a review lifecycle: employees create draft timesheets that automatically include all timelogs for the week, submit them for review, and receive approval or rejection from managers. Approved timesheets lock all included timelogs to prevent modifications, while rejected timesheets return to draft status for correction.

Referenced by {@link HrmTimesheetTimelogs} for the many-to-many relationship with individual timelogs.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each timesheet record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_employee_id
reviewed_by

plainFields.name: week_start_date
plainFields.description:
The Monday date marking the start of the weekly period covered by this timesheet.

Used for grouping timelogs and preventing duplicate submissions for the same week.

plainFields.name: week_end_date
plainFields.description:
The Sunday date marking the end of the weekly period covered by this timesheet.

Calculated as week_start_date + 6 days.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current workflow state of the timesheet.

Allowed values: draft, submitted, approved, rejected.

- draft: Initial state, timelogs can be modified
- submitted: Awaiting review, timelogs locked
- approved: Reviewed and approved, timelogs permanently locked
- rejected: Returned to employee for correction, returns to draft state

plainFields.name: total_hours
plainFields.description:
Sum of all timelog durations included in this timesheet, expressed in hours.

Calculated from the hrm_timesheet_timelogs junction table.

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timesheet was submitted for review.

Nullable for draft status. Populated when status transitions to submitted.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timesheet was reviewed (approved or rejected).

Nullable until review occurs. Populated when status transitions to approved or rejected.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description:
Reason provided when a timesheet is rejected.

Nullable for non-rejected statuses. Required when status is rejected.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timesheet was soft-deleted.

Nullable; null indicates active record.

models.name: hrm_timesheet_timelogs
models.description:
Junction table linking timesheets to timelogs for flexible inclusion.

This table enables many-to-many relationship between {@link hrm_timesheets} and {@link hrm_timelogs}, allowing timesheets to include specific timelog entries for weekly summaries and approval workflows. Each timesheet can contain multiple timelogs, and each timelog can be associated with multiple timesheets during draft and revision stages.

**Relationships**

- Links to {@link hrm_timesheets} via timesheet_id
- Links to {@link hrm_timelogs} via timelog_id

**Constraints**

- Composite unique constraint prevents duplicate timesheet-timelog pairs
- Both foreign keys are required (NOT NULL)
- Soft delete support via deleted_at field

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the junction record.

foreignFields.name: timesheet_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the timesheet that includes this timelog.

Links to {@link hrm_timesheets}. This foreign key establishes the parent timesheet context for the included timelog entry.

foreignFields.name: timelog_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the timelog entry included in the timesheet.

Links to {@link hrm_timelogs}. This foreign key identifies the specific time tracking record being included in the timesheet summary.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this junction record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this junction record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this junction record was soft-deleted.

models.name: hrm_active_timers
models.description:
Live timer sessions tracking ongoing work with start timestamp.

Each employee can have at most one active timer at a time, ensuring accurate real-time tracking of current work activities. When a timer is stopped, it creates a {@link hrm_timelogs} entry with calculated duration. Discarding a timer deletes the record without creating a timelog.

**Relationships**

- {@link hrm_employees} - The employee actively tracking time
- {@link hrm_projects} - The project being worked on
- {@link hrm_tasks} - Optional specific task within the project

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each active timer session.

foreignFields.name: employee_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the employee actively tracking time.

Each employee can have at most one active timer at a time, enforced by a unique constraint on this field. When the timer is stopped, this employee is credited with the recorded time in a {@link hrm_timelogs} entry.

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the project the employee is currently working on.

This links the timer session to a specific project for time tracking and reporting purposes. The project must belong to the same organization as the employee.

foreignFields.name: task_id
foreignFields.description:
Optional reference to the specific task within the project being worked on.

Allows granular time tracking at the task level. When null, time is tracked at the project level only. The task must belong to the referenced project.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Optional description of the current work activity.

Provides context for what the employee is working on during this timer session. This description will be copied to the {@link hrm_timelogs} entry when the timer is stopped.

plainFields.name: start_timestamp
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timer was started.

Used to calculate the elapsed duration when the timer is stopped. Duration is rounded to the nearest minute for the resulting {@link hrm_timelogs} entry.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timer record was created, typically matching start_timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timer record was last updated, used for concurrency control and audit purposes.

models.name: hrm_activity_logs
models.description:
Audit trail of significant actions across all domains with user, action type, and target entity information.

This table records system-wide activity events for compliance and debugging purposes. Each entry captures who performed an action, what type of action it was, and which entity was affected. The append-only design ensures an immutable historical record of all significant system events.

Actions logged include employee invitations and status changes, contract modifications, project lifecycle events, task status transitions, timesheet workflow changes, and role assignments. Users can query logs by action type, user, or date range for auditing and troubleshooting.

The polymorphic target_entity_type and target_entity_id fields allow this single table to reference entities across all domain components without requiring foreign keys to each specific table.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the activity log entry.

foreignFields.name: hrm_members_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the user who performed the action.

This foreign key links the activity log to the {@link hrm_members} table, identifying which authenticated user triggered the logged event. For system-generated actions, this field may reference a system service account.

plainFields.name: timestamp
plainFields.description:
When the action occurred.

Captures the exact moment the logged event happened, independent of when the log entry was created. This allows for accurate chronological ordering of events even if log entries are written asynchronously.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description:
Type of action performed.

Enumerates the category of business event being logged. Examples include: employee_invited, employee_deactivated, employee_reactivated, contract_created, contract_edited, project_created, project_archived, project_completed, project_deleted, task_status_changed, timesheet_submitted, timesheet_approved, timesheet_rejected, role_assigned, role_changed.

plainFields.name: target_entity_type
plainFields.description:
Type of entity that was targeted by the action.

Identifies the domain entity class affected by the action (e.g., "Employee", "Project", "Task", "Timesheet", "Contract", "Role"). Used in conjunction with target_entity_id to form a polymorphic reference to the affected entity.

plainFields.name: target_entity_id
plainFields.description:
ID of the targeted entity.

The primary key of the entity affected by the action. Combined with target_entity_type, this forms a polymorphic reference. Nullable for actions that do not target a specific entity (e.g., system-wide events).

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description:
JSON-formatted details about the action.

Contains contextual information about the event, including before/after values for changed fields, additional metadata, and any relevant context. The structure varies by action_type and is documented in the activity logging specification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this log entry was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this log entry was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this log entry was soft-deleted. Audit logs are typically retained indefinitely, but soft delete support allows for compliance-driven data removal when required.
